Question
========
Double buffering is used to do what?


Answerlist
----------
* Reduce cache misses
* Proceed while I/O is happening
* Increase the size of virtual memory
* Ensure the user cannot overwrite the data before it is sent

Solution
========
While one buffer is being transferred to the device, the application fills the other one, so computation and I/O overlap. It also guarantees that the buffer handed to the device is not modified under its feet while the transfer is in flight.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. Using two buffers rather increases the memory footprint.
* 1. One buffer is in flight while the other is being filled, so the two overlap.
* 0. Unrelated to the size of the address space.
* 1. The buffer being transferred is left untouched until the device is done with it.
